newsitem.title: UK: Copper heading lower in 1997 and 1998 - Billiton.
newsitem.headline: Copper heading lower in 1997 and 1998 - Billiton.

text.p: Copper prices are foreacst to fall in 1997 and 1998 as a modest rise in Western world demand fails to absorb a flood of new metal coming on stream over the period, Billiton Metals said in their weekly report.

Billiton forecast cash copper prices to fall to an average of 90 cents per pound ($1,984/tonne) in 1997 from 103 cents ($2,271) in 1996. The market is expected to drop sharply again in 1998 to an average of 75 cents ($1,653).
Supply is expected to outstrip demand in the West next year by 400,000 tonnes, and by 450,000 tonnes in 1998. The surplus was much smaller at 75,000 tonnes in 1996, Billiton said.
"In our view this surge in output next year will occur against a backdrop of reasonable but unspectaular demand growth," Billiton said.
The report said the market may remain tight during the first part of 1997 as Japan steps up its buying as a part of the GSP import round.
And China remained a wild card which could be critical to the Western world market, it added.
But on balance supply should get easier and prices softer.
"We look for a steady increase in stocks as the year (1997) wears on," the report concluded.
